title: Upper bound for noise sensitivity
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\delta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\delta\leq\tfrac12$. The noise sensitivity defined by $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)=\bigl(1-\operatorname{Stab}_{1-2\delta}(f)\bigr)/2$ satisfies $$\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)\leq\frac12.$$
replaced:
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, real-valued $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\mathbb R$ and real $\delta\leq1/2$, including negative $\delta$, the total real-valued noise sensitivity satisfies
\[
\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)=\frac{1-\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}(1-2\delta)^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^2}{2}\leq\frac12,
\]
where $\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}}f(x)\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$.
